title: Two-tier and three-tier applications
purpose: Compare direct client application database calls with middle application-server tier.
alt: 클라이언트의 직접 DB 호출과 애플리케이션 서버를 경유하는 2계층·3계층 비교
requiredChecks: Two-tier has user/application in Client tier connected directly over network to Database server.
Three-tier has UI/application client→Application server→Database server, all three tiers separately labelled.
Three-tier UI has no direct Database server link.
User boxes are not mistaken for separate server tiers; application server performs DB calls.
prompt: Create a new original English raster technical diagram for an IT study blog. White background, flat blue and teal cards, navy large sans-serif text, generous whitespace, clean orthogonal connectors, no logos or copied textbook composition. All labels readable and uncropped. Title "Two-tier and three-tier applications". Two side-by-side panels, left "Two-tier", right "Three-tier". LEFT vertical: bounded "Client tier" containing "User interface + application", downward doubleheaded link label "Database calls / results" through thin horizontal "Network" separator, bounded "Database tier" containing "Database server". RIGHT vertical THREE separate boundaries: "Client tier" contains "User interface / application client", bidirectional arrow label "Requests / responses" through Network separator to "Application tier" containing "Application server", bidirectional arrow label "Database calls / results" to "Database tier" containing "Database server". No rightclient→DB shortcut. Footer left "Application calls the database directly"; footer right "Application server mediates database access". Keep panels independent, no connectors across panels.
